text: You're in the supermarket, list in hand. Just trying to grab your groceries, find good value, and get out quickly.
But as your eyes scan the shelves, you notice something. The items that jump out, right at your level, often seem pricier.
You might think these are just popular brands. But finding a cheaper alternative usually means bending low or stretching high for it.
This isn't random. It's a calculated strategy: 'eye-level is buy-level.' Retailers know this is prime real estate for impulse buys.
They place their most profitable items exactly where your gaze naturally lands. Your desire for convenience makes you spend more, invisibly.
Next time, you'll see this system at work. Scan every shelf, up and down. The best deals are often hiding, just not at eye level.
